## Trial `password-complexity-policy-ubunt__ZQne4Mg`

**Verifier decision: Full Success.** Both material requirements -- minimum 12-character length and at least 3 character classes for new/self-service user passwords on node1 -- are directly demonstrated as enforced via libpam-pwquality/pwquality.conf, with rejection and acceptance tests both before and after a full node reboot proving persistence. Test users were fully cleaned up and no residue or failed services remain. The task was completed cleanly with no unnecessary mutations.

| Reward | Coverage | Functionality | Hygiene | Confidence | Commands |

| 1.000 | 1.000 | 1.000 | 0.950 | 0.950 | 22/3 |

### Why the verifier reached this decision

- **min-length-12 — Satisfied:** New user passwords on node1 must be at least 12 characters long
  - **Why:** libpam-pwquality installed and wired into /etc/pam.d/common-password ahead of pam_unix; pwquality.conf set minlen=12. Self-service password change with a shorter password (8-9 chars) was directly rejected with 'password is shorter than 12 characters' both before (cmd-fd1d94daad9d429f) and after a full reboot (cmd-3d25a26e26a94291), and a compliant 14-char password was accepted (cmd-a11b60314b1343f9).
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-a77812fe996a4a42`, `cmd-909775d8123244f4`, `cmd-fd1d94daad9d429f`, `cmd-3d25a26e26a94291`, `cmd-a11b60314b1343f9`
- **min-classes-3 — Satisfied:** New user passwords on node1 must use at least three different character classes
  - **Why:** pwquality.conf set minclass=3. Self-service change to a 14-char, all-lowercase-plus-digit password (2 classes) was directly rejected with 'password contains less than 3 character classes' (cmd-aa2eba635bce4151); the same compliant password with upper/lower/digit/symbol (4 classes) was accepted (cmd-a11b60314b1343f9). Config persisted after reboot (cmd-5816a2de9b7a44f6).
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-a77812fe996a4a42`, `cmd-aa2eba635bce4151`, `cmd-a11b60314b1343f9`, `cmd-5816a2de9b7a44f6`
- **policy-persistence — Satisfied:** Policy must persist across a restart (bonus/expected robustness given mandatory restart evidence protocol)
  - **Why:** Boot identity changed from 2dffe735-... to cebf3731-... across a reboot (cmd-c6b2c629647540e6, cmd-1b2f6f4cdc30470c, cmd-a76d00fda4de40b3), confirmed by the fixed lifecycle snapshots (global:before_prepare:node1:boot-identity vs global:after_executor:node1:boot-identity). PAM stack ordering and pwquality.conf settings were re-verified intact post-reboot (cmd-5816a2de9b7a44f6), and live enforcement was re-validated with a fresh test user rejecting a too-short password (cmd-3d25a26e26a94291).
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-c6b2c629647540e6`, `cmd-2641e970a1e7472e`, `cmd-1b2f6f4cdc30470c`, `cmd-a76d00fda4de40b3`, `cmd-5816a2de9b7a44f6`, `cmd-3d25a26e26a94291`, `global:before_prepare:node1:boot-identity`, `global:after_executor:node1:boot-identity`

### Comments and limitations

- Root-set passwords (via `passwd <user>` as root) bypass pwquality enforcement per standard PAM/Linux behavior (visible in cmd-20038d2db7f3407e, cmd-1e46aecd6dd74be8, cmd-cd6e830a38764ea7); only self-service passwd changes were shown to be enforced. This is expected root-override behavior, not a policy gap, but was not explicitly called out as intentional by the executor.
- Verification relied on two ephemeral test users created and deleted by the executor rather than inspection of any pre-existing account; this is a reasonable and low-risk approach but means no real end-user password change was observed.
- Operational hygiene was below a full pass (0.950); review the hygiene explanation above separately from functional success.
- Verifier confidence was 0.950; this is evidence confidence for this trial, not a repeatability estimate.
